answer: Each agent posts a bond locked to one hardware-attested human. Running twenty "independent" agents therefore needs twenty separate bonds, and any pair proven to share an origin is slashed. Identity alone is cheap: one human could mint endless agents. The bond fixes that, because extra agents divide one scarce stake instead of multiplying it. A vine's leaves all feed from a single root, so one cut reaches everything. Collusion shows in a falcon-sharp correlation of timing and shared fingerprints, the bridge from trust to money.
